master:
Use case: historical-scene. Create a magnificent production keyframe for a 60-second cinematic Waterloo 1815 film, VERTICAL 9:16, very high resolution. This is a sophisticated layered PAPER-CUT LIGHTBOX artwork, hand-cut painted matte paper, not a realistic battlefield photograph. Entire composition must share one perspective, one palette, one illumination and one tactile paper material.

COMPOSITION: monumental low viewpoint from a hillside overlooking vast battle lines. At lower left a single French Imperial Guard standard bearer in 1815 dark navy coat and bearskin hat, seen in three-quarter back profile facing towards the right and distant battlefield. He must be substantial in scale (occupying roughly the lower 35 percent in height), clearly shaped, historically plausible, with restrained engraved lines embossed into colored paper to show coat folds, belts and boots. His gloved hand actually grips the pole. A beautifully cut golden Napoleonic eagle standard rises above him near upper-left center; the unlettered blue-white-red flag is moderately sized and folds towards the right. The pole length must be proportionate to a full-size bearer, not a tiny man under an oversized banner. One foreground figure only. Crisp paper edges, subtle edge thickness and local layered relief, no glossy sculptural shading.

MIDGROUND: broad diagonal terraces of slate-blue, dusty olive and muted ochre paper hills, with simplified dark single-color infantry silhouettes and several distinctive waving standards. No detailed faces in the middle. Keep a clear breathing zone around the near bearer.

DISTANT: truly gigantic army scale. Thousands upon thousands of tiny dark bayonet and shako silhouettes in long sweeping columns and regiment ribbons across the upper middle, continuing off both edges and disappearing towards the far horizon. Dense but orderly masses across a broad valley, small flags like a forest above them. Indicate armies through recognizable coherent layered silhouette masses, not detailed crowds. Two opposing forces, atmospheric separation and one tiny distant Belgian farmhouse. The distant battlefield and sky together must feel endless, not a toy shelf.

LIGHT AND BEAUTY: luminous warm amber and ivory light transmitted from behind, cool deep Prussian blue in the shadows, muted oxblood accents. Multiple visibly separated cut-paper planes with narrow soft layer shadows and fine bevel highlights. A large dramatic storm cloud made of sweeping cut-paper layers above, with amber backlight breaking through near the horizon and theatrical crepuscular rays. Sky has purposeful sculptural cloud shapes, no large blank flat gradient. Restrained subtle paper fibers. Strong chiaroscuro, solemn epic atmosphere, refined museum-quality craft, tasteful cinematic composition. Foreground should feel the same art as the army and landscape; no pasted sticker appearance.

No lettering anywhere: no title, caption, date, symbols resembling text, watermark, flag inscriptions, readable insignia or logo. No modern equipment, no explosions, no firing flashes, no borders, no arched window frame. Historical dramatic illustration, not documentary evidence.

layers.prompt: Edit target: the supplied Waterloo layered-paper lightbox keyframe. Extract ONLY the entire large foreground French standard bearer, his complete boots/coat/head/hand, his complete eagle-topped pole and blue-white-red flag, and the cut-paper rocky/grassy foreground hill he is standing on along the bottom edge. Remove absolutely all sky, clouds, distant landscapes, small soldiers, buildings and distant flags. Output actual transparent alpha. Preserve exactly the source subject's proportions, pose, intricate matte painted-paper colors, edge thickness, warm upper-right backlight, and relative canvas coordinates. Keep the same 9:16 canvas and original scale/composition; the foreground hill may still span the entire bottom edge. Do not create an extra ground halo, new cast shadow, duplicate pole, extra limbs, text or checkerboard.

Edit target: supplied Waterloo layered-paper lightbox keyframe. Create a matching clean BACKGROUND PLATE by removing only the large foreground French standard bearer, all of his pole/eagle/blue-white-red flag, and the near dark rocky/grassy mound along the bottom edge. Reveal and complete the valley terraces and distant army ribbons where those near elements stood. Preserve the existing enormous army scale, far tiny silhouette rows and flags, luminous storm paper sky, landscape perspective and all its colors, matte textured paper relief and backlight. The resulting scene has no large near person, no large near horse, no large near artillery and no border. Distant armies are small flat silhouette shapes. Full 9:16 artwork filled edge to edge. No words or inscriptions anywhere. Do not turn into a photo or oil painting.

style: Layered paper lightbox; detailed foreground, solid midground, monumental distant armies
